item.title: Record cyclosporiasis outbreak tests agencies hit by Trump administration's cuts
item.description: Last year's funding cuts to federal agencies that oversee foodborne illness outbreaks are being tested with the record cyclosporiasis outbreak in the U.S.

item.title: Doctors say Medicaid change to gender-affirming care will harm vulnerable youth
item.description: Federal Medicaid dollars can no longer pay for gender-affirming care for youth. Doctors who treat trans kids say it will harm vulnerable people.
item.content:encoded: Federal Medicaid dollars can no longer pay for gender-affirming care for youth. Doctors who treat trans kids say it will harm vulnerable people.

item.title: The drug lenacapavir is a mighty weapon against HIV. Its rollout gets mixed reviews
item.description: It's a twice-a-year injection that is remarkably effective in preventing an HIV infection. Distribution is starting. But questions are being raised about getting it to the areas that need it most.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Boston-area trial draws attention to post-partum psychosis
item.description: A mom is on trial for killing her children. Her defense says she had post-partum psychosis. Psychiatrists hope the case brings attention to the need for better diagnosis and treatment for the illness.

item.title: His wedding guests gave $6k to fund a health startup. Now it's won a $3 million prize
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi founded Last Mile Health to bring healthcare to people living in remote areas. The group is the 2026 recipient of the Conrad N. Hilton Humanitarian Prize.

item.title: Feel so busy you don't even realize you're busy? Try doing a time audit
item.description: The exercise can help you identify what's wasting your time — and make room for what matters, says psychotherapist Niro Feliciano. Take a moment to try it. You might be surprised with what you find.

item.title: Nuclear power push ramps up uranium mill — and tribal health concerns

item.title: A midwife crosses 'maternity deserts' to make a difference for Black moms and babies
item.description: New research from the March of Dimes says more than half of U.S. counties have no labor and delivery hospitals. One Black midwife tries to make a difference for moms in Alabama.

item.title: Fewer resources and funding cuts contributing to spike in foodborne illnesses
item.description: It's been a bad summer for foodborne illnesses -- from a record-breaking cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to iceberg lettuce to salmonella infections linked to jalapeños.
